parsedVerdict.reasoning: The repositories module should hold one concern: persisting Task entities through repository implementations. CircularB.ts is a general console logger (`log(msg)` calls `console.log`). It has nothing to do with persistence, so the module covers two unrelated concerns. InMemoryTaskRepository creates `private readonly helper = new CircularB()` but never calls it. That makes CircularB dead coupling, not a real collaborator. CircularB also imports InMemoryTaskRepository and never uses it. I did not count the circular import itself, because import direction is out of scope; I cite it only to show the two files are not a coherent unit. InMemoryTaskRepository also skips the module's own abstraction. The source comment says it 'Does NOT implement ITaskRepository', so the class is a free-standing class instead of an implementation of the domain's repository port. Its use cases then get it by constructor injection (the graph shows `CreateTaskUseCase` CONSTRUCTOR_INJECTS InMemoryTaskRepository) rather than through the interface. Smaller inconsistency: `findByPriority(_priority)` ignores its argument and returns every task. It implies a priority filter that the repository does not apply.

violations.message: CircularB is a general console logger (`log(msg)`) that has nothing to do with Task persistence, so it doesn't belong in the repositories module. It also imports InMemoryTaskRepository and never uses it.

InMemoryTaskRepository does not implement the ITaskRepository port, which skips the module's repository abstraction. It also creates an unused `helper = new CircularB()`, tying it to an unrelated logging concern.
`findByPriority(_priority)` ignores its argument and returns every task. The method name promises a priority filter that the repository does not apply.
